meta.title: Competitor Radar
meta.niche: Conversion tracking and attribution platforms for performance marketers (server-side tracking, Conversion API feeds to ad platforms)

analysis.summary: Almost nobody published in the last 30 days. Only RedTrack and Triple Whale showed any activity, and both are small signals.

points.text: Four of the five rivals, AnyTrack included, published and updated nothing in 30 days, so the space is quiet right now.
RedTrack updated 4 older pages, including 2 case studies. That looks like a small refresh, not a new push.
Triple Whale updated two AI-in-ecommerce guides and added one BFCM (Black Friday/Cyber Monday) training page. Its focus is brand education, not tracking.

AnyTrack.play: No new or updated pages in 30 days. Large site of 1182 pages plus 140 integration pages.

Hyros.play: No activity in 30 days. Site has 137 pages.

RedTrack.play: Refreshed 2 case studies and a cookieless tracking page, plus an AI agents list.

Voluum.play: No activity in 30 days. Site has 319 pages.

Triple Whale.play: Updated AI-for-ecommerce guides and launched a BFCM certification page. Also has 182 expert pages.

Northbeam.play: No activity in 30 days. Site has 205 pages.

shared.title: AI-for-ecommerce lists
shared.text: RedTrack and Triple Whale each updated a 'best AI tools/agents for ecommerce' page. They want search traffic from the AI topic, which sits beside tracking. AnyTrack has no visible page there.

gaps.title: Server-side tracking how-tos
gaps.text: No rival published a tracking guide this month. AnyTrack could own Conversion API setup content for media buyers while rivals chase AI topics.

gaps.title: Fresh customer case studies
gaps.text: Only RedTrack refreshed case studies (2). AnyTrack could publish new proof stories of better ad-platform conversion feeds.

gaps.title: Certification or training programs
gaps.text: Only Triple Whale has a training page (BFCM Certified). Nobody offers certification for tracking and attribution. AnyTrack could own that.

versus.Hyros: Also silent this month, with a much smaller site (137 pages) than AnyTrack's 1182.
versus.RedTrack: More active than AnyTrack: it refreshed 4 pages and leans on case studies and cookieless tracking, while AnyTrack showed nothing.
versus.Voluum: Also silent this month. Its site is about a quarter the size of AnyTrack's.
versus.Triple Whale: Similar site size to AnyTrack, but it is active, with training and AI content aimed at ecommerce brands, not media buyers.
versus.Northbeam: Also silent this month, with a site (205 pages) far smaller than AnyTrack's.
